script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: The statement that Israel and Jacob are the same person needs a reference to a verse that says so outright, such as Genesis 35:10.
Judah says they will not go without their brother once, not twice. He repeats the man's warning.
“No guards in this story” asserts more than the passage says. It does not mention Judah hiring guards.
The shortcut comparison does not match Judah's point about delaying the trip. It describes discovering a shorter route after taking a longer one.
The text does not say that wool, barley and dates stayed home. They are simply not on Israel's gift list.
Israel says, “May God Almighty grant you mercy.” The explanation turns his words to his sons into an asserted request to God.
The text records Israel saying, “May God Almighty grant you mercy”; it does not describe him praying.
“Israel isn't sure of anything” overstates what the text says, and the claim that nobody would say those words when certain asserts an unsupported rule about people's feelings.
“Then he says” places Israel's words after he sends the sons, but he says them before they depart.
The passage does not say whether the brothers know about the meal when Joseph gives the order.
The brothers are taken to Joseph's house before the noon meal, so saying nobody is being sent anywhere before lunch is inaccurate.
Identifying Reuben as another of Jacob's sons needs a reference outside this passage, such as Genesis 29:32.
Identifying Levi as another of Jacob's sons needs a reference outside this passage, such as Genesis 29:34.
“I'll keep my jokes out of it” comments on how Papa is telling the passage.
The text says the groups were served separately, but it does not say there were three tables.
“My brothers” gives Papa brothers, even in the imagined comparison. His only family members are his six cookie cutter kids.
The explanation presents cookies on the brothers' plates as part of the scene. The passage does not say they ate cookies; the comparison needs to be clearly hypothetical.
The text describes the size of Benjamin's portion, not the size of his plate.
The text says Benjamin's portion was larger, not that he received the biggest plate.
